reason: The sandboxed run: one agent on boost (live/madelon-fleet3-boost), with every command in the bwrap sandbox of spec 8, for the launcher's wall clock of 1,800 seconds. The trail checks. Nothing is resolved, and boost stays open. The agent read the map once, surveyed the workspace it started from, and wrote a pilot-only search over four screens (step-11). Its run at step-12 was still going when the wall clock stopped it, so that run has no observation. The file trace is why. The first screen took 701 seconds under the trace. I ran the same command without the trace on a copy of the workspace: 52 seconds, with the same result (nested AUC 0.6598). Two of the four screens had finished when the session ended. What the sandbox did, with a model for the first time: uv, Python and git worked inside it; the note at step-1 lists what was hidden; no command names a path outside the workspace or reaches the network, by a reading of all four commands; no run opened data/heldout.csv, by the trace of the three that settled; and no process outlived the session. It is the first trail of this map that never opened the held-out file. What this does not show: an agent trying to leave the sandbox, or a held-out score from a sandboxed run.

routes.why: Five pilot-only designs of a screen and an RBF SVM gave nested cross-validated AUCs of 0.66 to 0.68 (madelon-route-svm steps 19 to 33), under the forest's 0.7267 on the same screen, and the agent's last plan expected a held-out AUC under the floor. The run stopped at the token ceiling before scoring the held-out file, so compact-svm is neither reached nor refuted.
